title: Reviewing previously taught names and memory links
summary: Anchored to the XC030 name-recall exchange: review previously taught names, accept partial retrieval, ask how a name was remembered, and offer a relevant association. The opening retains the source review premise while removing the food-topic transition and mute instruction. Reference answers are therapist-only material; the text runner does not reconstruct the prior lesson or pictures.

therapist.context: Continue the review activity from the source: the session premise is that two pictured people and name-memory strategies were introduced last week. Begin by inviting recall of the woman, then the man, and discuss the method that helped. The current text runner does not supply the earlier lesson or photographs; this premise sets the conversation topic, not evidence of what this patient remembers. Accept a patient who does not recognize the exercise and clarify without inventing an image or insisting that they learned it.
objectives: Invite recall of previously taught names before offering a name or an association, following the original review sequence.
Support partial or uncertain responses with manageable cues while distinguishing cues from a supplied answer.
Ask what helped the patient connect a name with its association, using their actual response.
materials: Therapist reference answer for the woman: Tan Mei Li. The original teaching linked mei li with beautiful in Chinese. Keep the answer private until the patient has attempted recall or asks for help; no photograph is supplied by this runner.

Therapist reference answer for the man: Lim Chong Wei. The original association links Chong Wei with badminton player Lee Chong Wei but uses the surname Lim. Use this only as responsive support, not as an opening presentation of the answer.

Treat capitalization, punctuation, spacing, and clearly recognizable spoken or transliteration variations flexibly. A correct given name with a missing surname is partial recall. Reversed given-name order can be clarified gently rather than treated as a wholly unrelated answer.

A reminder of the verbal association is a cue. Stating the complete target name is providing the answer. A subsequent repetition demonstrates repetition after teaching, not recall before the answer was given.
therapist.opening_question: Last week we practised some strategies for remembering these people's names. Can you remember this lady's name?
conversation_plan: Start with the source-based review question without first teaching or listing the answers. Respond to the woman-name attempt; clarify uncertainty or offer one cue only if needed.
Invite an attempt at the man's name, as in the source follow-up: And this gentleman? Allow a partial name or an explicit inability to recall.
When a name has been recalled, ask how the patient remembered it. If it was not recalled, ask which part is difficult rather than assuming a successful method.
Respond to the patient's explanation. Offer or reinforce an appropriate association only at this point, keeping a cue distinct from a full answer.
Briefly summarize the method actually discussed. Accept that an offered association may not help and that some items may remain unresolved.
response_guidance: Do not expect a particular error, success, confidence level, or explanation from the patient.

The case supplies the prior-session review premise, not this patient's prior responses. If the patient says they did not attend, cannot identify the people, or lacks the material, acknowledge and clarify; do not insist they learned it or invent a past answer. Do not assume familiarity with badminton or Chinese.
Do not claim to show a face or infer visual recognition. Do not ask about facial features that have not been supplied.

Keep track of the name parts and cues you actually supply. Do not call an answer independent recall after supplying it, and do not infer retention of a prior lesson that this runner has not reconstructed.
Use task questions as well as a brief strategy discussion; do not turn every turn into a broad counseling question.
completion_criteria: The woman and man name targets have been discussed or explicitly set aside, including when the patient lacks the prior task context.
The dialogue establishes at least one reported useful link, an identified difficulty, or that the offered association did not help.
Any closing feedback accurately reflects the support given and does not assert improvement that was not demonstrated.
reference_utterances: So how do you remember Tan Mei Li's name?
So that's a way of linking up.

selection.rule: Use the most recent explicitly dated Home Visit assessment before the source recording; keep baseline demographics separately attributed. Do not use future visits or target-response content.
selection.moca_score_policy: Keep recorded totals and subitems without repeat education adjustment. Set conflicting runtime fields to null and retain their original values and related cells in provenance.
selection.dass_score_policy: Use only the selected visit totals; preserve the recorded scale and do not infer diagnostic categories.
